groups.name: stx.workflow
groups.description: The stx-workflow engine, over the WorkflowStore bean.

groups.name: stx.workflow.worker
groups.description: The worker that picks up instances nobody is advancing.

properties.name: stx.workflow.enabled
properties.description: Build an stx-workflow engine over the WorkflowStore bean, registering every Workflow bean with it. Off by default.

properties.name: stx.workflow.store
properties.description: Which store to build instances in: redis, jpa or mongo, each over the connection the matching stx.* group already opened. Unset means build none, because the application declares a WorkflowStore bean of its own. Nothing is inferred: an application with both a Redis and a Jpa bean is not saying where its instances belong.

properties.name: stx.workflow.lease
properties.description: How long an instance lock is good for before the instance is assumed abandoned. Default 30s. Not a deadline on a step: the lock renews while the work runs. Ignored when the application declares its own WorkflowStore.

properties.name: stx.workflow.retention
properties.description: How long a finished instance is kept before it is expired. Default 7d. A Failed instance is exempt whatever this says: it is waiting for a person, and expiring it would delete the only description of what needs fixing. Ignored by the jpa store, where a table has no TTL and retention is JpaWorkflowStore.purge on a schedule the application owns.

properties.name: stx.workflow.child-poll
properties.description: How often a parent parked on a child node looks at the child again. Default 1m. A safety net rather than the mechanism: a child resumes its parent the moment it finishes, and this only covers a process that died between those two writes. It needs stx.workflow.worker.enabled, or an application scheduler calling resume; nothing polls on its own.

properties.name: stx.workflow.worker.enabled
properties.description: Run a WorkflowWorker in this process, picking up instances nobody is advancing. Off by default: enabling stx.workflow gives an application a way to run workflows, and whether this process also recovers the fleet's abandoned ones is a separate decision.

properties.name: stx.workflow.worker.poll
properties.description: How long the worker waits between two looks at an empty index. Default 1s. A java.time.Duration (1s, PT1S): the binder has never heard of kotlin.time.Duration.

properties.name: stx.workflow.worker.batch
properties.description: How many due instances the worker takes at a time.

properties.name: stx.workflow.worker.concurrency
properties.description: How many instances the worker advances at once.
